summary.oneLiner: Jaro delivered strong Q3FY26 execution with 42% YoY revenue growth and EBITDA profitability after prior losses, driven by higher ARPU (up 2x in 4 years), referral-led customer acquisition (35-36%), and strategic partnerships with IITs/IIMs; what matters is the sustainable margin trajectory (EBITDA 26% for 9M) and scalable model without cash burn, positioning it as India’s only consistently profitable EdTech platform.

one-line thesis: Jaro delivered strong Q3FY26 execution with 42% YoY revenue growth and EBITDA profitability after prior losses, driven by higher ARPU (up 2x in 4 years), referral-led customer acquisition (35-36%), and strategic partnerships with IITs/IIMs; what matters is the sustainable margin trajectory (EBITDA 26% for 9M) and scalable model without cash burn, positioning it as India’s only consistently profitable EdTech platform.
financial scorecard: revenue: +42% YoY to INR61.8cr (Q3); +13.29% YoY to INR203cr (9M); EBITDA/margin: turned profitable at INR12.29cr (Q3) vs loss in Q3FY25; 9M EBITDA INR53.05cr (26.12% margin); PAT (rptd): INR7.03cr (Q3), INR31.58cr (9M); PAT (normalized): same as reported; order book: not disclosed; net debt: strong cash position maintained, no debt mentioned
guidance: revenue growth: 20-25% FY26; margin: targeting EBITDA >30%, PAT >19-20%; order inflow: no explicit target, but J.K. Shah partnership to drive volume from April; capex/commissioning: 17 studios already deployed, no new capex guidance
segment / subsidiary detail: Corporate upskilling (IITs/IIMs/Symbiosis): 30% higher fee programs (INR2-9L); J.K. Shah commerce vertical: 4.2M TAM, online-only, same margin as peers; Jio ecosystem: free access via set-top boxes; School Connect (IIT Madras): new vertical targeting school children
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Tier 2/3 cities (Kolkata, Indore); J.K. Shah partnership (4.2M commerce learners); potential entry into content development if UGC permits; School Connect vertical for K-12; Jio ecosystem reach
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved to 26.12% (9M) due to reduced CAC via 35-36% referral rate; marketing spend optimized; fixed cost leverage from 17 studios; ARPU doubling (INR43k→84k) driven by shift to higher fee programs (30% of mix)
capex / expansion: INR17 studios deployed across IIMs (e.g., IIM Trichy: 5 studios); capex funded internally; no new capex guidance
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic growth via referrals and institutional partnerships; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; strong cash position enables future M&A or content development if regulatory shift occurs
risks & watch-items: Regulatory risk if UGC restricts third-party content development; over-reliance on institutional partners; execution risk in scaling J.K. Shah partnership; potential margin pressure if CAC rises due to new market entry
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, bootstrapped mindset; emphasis on profitability over growth-at-all-costs; proud of 17-year track record of consistent profits and zero cash burn; tone is founder-led, human-capital-centric
non-obvious takeaways: 35-36% of new enrollments come from learner referrals — a rare, defensible moat in EdTech; Jaro’s studios are embedded inside IIM campuses, creating institutional lock-in; Jio partnership gives free access to 100M+ Jio Fiber users — a stealth distribution channel

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Founded in 2009, Jaro Education is an early and established edtech player in India, focused on expanding access to quality higher education and professional upskilling beyond traditional campuses."
- Acts as "an end-to-end enabler, managing the complete programme lifecycle from admissions and learner outreach to technology-enabled delivery, bridging institutions and learners at scale" — a fee-sharing model rather than a degree-granting one.
- "Why Jaro Wins" rests on four claims: deep institutional partnerships enabling "program co-creation", business intelligence on learner demand, an integrated platform across "program design, acquisition, and delivery", and proven revenue generation for partner institutions via a dedicated sales team.
- Investment case is stated as "Scalable, asset-light model", "Favorable unit economics", "Operating leverage driving margin expansion", "Strong revenue visibility with long-duration programs" and "Recession free industry".
- Growth is described as a self-reinforcing loop: partnerships → business intelligence → portfolio expansion → sales/counselling engine → learner acquisition → revenue share reinvested "to scale and strengthen capabilities".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [IPO] The deck references an IPO in September 2025 as the reason for the increased share capital; "Current Market Cap (as on 10th Aug 2026)" is shown alongside a figure of 1,023 Cr. in the same snapshot block.
- [Ecosystem] Partnered with ET Education as E-learning Partner for the 3rd ET Education Annual Education Summit 2026 (12 June 2026) and participated in the panel "Education to Economy: Powering India's $5 Trillion Future".
- [Milestone] "17 YEARS OF IMPACT, INNOVATION & INSPIRATION" — the company dates its journey "From a bold vision in 2009".
- [IR] Investor relations is outsourced to SAAA Consultants Pvt. Ltd.; Chairman & MD is Dr. Sanjay Salunkhe, CEO & Wholetime Director Ranjita Raman (with Jaro since 2010, IIM Ahmedabad alumna) and CFO Sankesh Mophe (since 2011, founding member).
